clue.text: Bird led to break through shell

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go through, i.e. into the middle of, the synonym for shell

parts.note: to shuck peas or oysters is to shell them

indicators.note: broken letters are rearranged, so the word led is jumbled

explanation.surface: A bird is led to break out through its eggshell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' sounds like a chick breaking its shell, but it is the anagram signal for 'led'; 'shell' is the verb, as in shelling peas.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelduck is a large, boldly marked duck of coasts and estuaries, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Scattered boxes at end of lane

indicators.note: at simply joins the two pieces in order

parts.note: a boxer who spars is practising boxing

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of lane

explanation.surface: Boxes lie scattered at the far end of a country lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like containers, but it is a verb: SPARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered, a synonym describing things spread out.

clue.text: Former pilot's staggering feat

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-husband

indicators.note: staggering letters lurch out of order and are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A retired pilot achieved an astonishing feat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering' reads as amazing, but it signals the anagram of PILOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold or daring deed, a synonym of feat.

clue.text: Dried out thus in City district, wearing old hat

indicators.note: the old-fashioned word wears the rest inside it like clothing

parts.note: something old hat is dated, out of fashion

indicators.note: the Latin word goes in the postcode letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as written

explanation.surface: A dried-out figure in a City district wears an old-fashioned hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' is an idiom meaning out of date, not headgear; 'wearing' and 'in' are both container signals, one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiccated means dried out, as in desiccated coconut.

clue.text: May come to be Chatham? Pitt can't wait!

indicators.note: the letters may come to form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pitt, made Earl of Chatham, is impatient for his elevation.
explanation.walkthrough: William Pitt the Elder became Earl of Chatham; 'May come to' signals the anagram of BE CHATHAM PITT.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ at the bit is to be restless and impatient, an idiom from a horse chewing its bit.

clue.text: Champion on horseback with influence

parts.note: a jockey who is riding is said to be up
to have a hold over someone is to have influence over them

explanation.surface: A champion rider sits on horseback, carrying some weight in the sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' is a verb here, not the winner it seems to be.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to support or defend it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Reportedly Miss Peachum's old college

indicators.note: reportedly indicates a word as it is heard said

parts.note: Polly Peachum is the heroine of Gay's The Beggar's Opera

explanation.surface: Polly Peachum is said to have attended a former college.
explanation.definitionFit: A poly is short for a polytechnic, a type of UK college that became a university in 1992.

clue.text: Neat Italian fellow admitted it produces rust

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

indicators.note: the Italian abbreviation has the fellow admitted into it

parts.note: Dan is a man's name standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A tidy Italian man confessed that it produces rust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' reads as tidy but is the old word for cattle. DAN is 'admitted' into IT, making IDANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxidant is a substance that oxidises others, and rust is iron oxide.

clue.text: Mutt left out of RAF unit's encounter

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: left is taken out of the word for the RAF unit

parts.note: a flight is a small unit of aircraft in the RAF

explanation.surface: A dog is left out of an RAF squadron's mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out of' reads as one phrase, but 'left' gives L and 'out of' removes it from FLIGHT, leaving FIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogfight is an aerial encounter between fighter planes.

clue.text: It contributed to Cleopatra's passing

indicators.note: the letters straddling the two words each contribute part of the run inside them

explanation.surface: A remark that something played a part in Cleopatra's death.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of Cleopatra's and the start of passing; the whole clue also describes the snake that killed her.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra is said to have died from the bite of an Egyptian cobra, a venomous snake.

clue.text: Builder's aid marketed outside snack bar in Gateshead

indicators.note: the word for marketed goes outside, around, the snack bar

parts.note: something sold has been marketed
a caff is British slang for a cheap cafe or snack bar
taken as written
read as gate's head, the first letter of gate; Gateshead is a town in north-east England

explanation.surface: A builder's material was sold outside a snack bar in the north-east town of Gateshead.
explanation.walkthrough: The town name Gateshead is split as 'gate's head', giving its first letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaffolding is the framework of poles and planks that helps builders reach upper storeys.

clue.text: One who hops overseas to get game?

parts.note: French stands for the foreign, across the Channel
a cricket is a hopping insect

explanation.surface: Someone who travels across the sea to play a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The insect comes first in the clue, but FRENCH leads the answer. French cricket is an informal garden game played with a bat and ball.
explanation.definitionFit: French cricket is a simplified children's ball game in which the batter's legs are the wicket.

clue.text: Like some peaks an English novelist improved on

parts.note: C. P. Snow was an English novelist, author of the Strangers and Brothers sequence
to cap a story is to improve on or outdo it

explanation.surface: An English writer bettered someone's description of mountain peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: High mountain peaks are often covered at the summit by white winter layers, a descriptive adjective.

clue.text: Vehicle appears to move along the ground

definitions.meaning: a cab hired with a driver for a fare
what an aircraft does when it rolls along the runway before take-off or after landing

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a hired cab; the other is an aircraft rolling on the runway under its own power.

clue.text: How the Lower House functions, being without equal

definitions.meaning: the Commons works without members of the House of Lords, i.e. without lords
unmatched, in a way nobody can rival

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the word means without lords; its normal sense is in an unmatched way.

clue.text: Sibelius's first characteristic passage

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the composer's name

parts.note: a characteristic is a trait or feature

explanation.surface: A passage in a Sibelius symphony typical of the Finnish composer's style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' suggests music, but it is a narrow sea channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow passage of water linking two seas.

clue.text: Spotted creature one that stings, some say

indicators.note: what some people say out loud signals a word of the same sound

parts.note: to sting is slang for to swindle, so one that stings is a swindler

explanation.surface: A spotted animal is described as something that stings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stings' suggests an insect, but it is slang for cheating someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is a big cat whose coat is covered with black spots.

clue.text: Irritable about note in Bible, a distortion

indicators.note: the irritable word goes about, around, the rest

parts.note: testy means irritable

indicators.note: the note goes in the Bible abbreviation

parts.note: RV is the Revised Version of the Bible
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: An irritable person complains about a note in a Bible translation as a distortion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a container signal here, not RE or C; the Bible is the Revised Version rather than the more familiar AV.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque misrepresentation, a synonym of distortion.

clue.text: One bound breaking woman's back —- need to revive

indicators.note: back, after 's (is), tells us the whole assembly is read in the opposite direction
the bound worker breaks into the woman's word, splitting it

parts.note: her is a pronoun standing for a woman
a serf was a person bound to the land, an unfree labourer

explanation.surface: Someone takes one leap, hurts a woman's back, and now needs reviving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One bound' looks like a single leap, but it means a man bound to the land; 'back' turns the whole assembly round after 'breaking' puts him inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh someone is to restore their energy, a synonym of revive.

clue.text: Apt criterion for the most healthy

parts.note: something apt is fit or suitable
a test is a standard by which something is judged

explanation.surface: A suitable standard is used to pick out the healthiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Fittest is the superlative of fit, meaning in the best physical condition.

clue.text: Box? He did a far, far better thing

definitions.text: He did a far, far better thing
definitions.meaning: Sydney ... last words in Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities, as he goes to the guillotine

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a cardboard box; the other is Dickens's hero Sydney who dies in another man's place.

clue.text: Nothing in a closed vehicle as source of music

indicators.note: the first three pieces close round, enclosing, the vehicle

parts.note: O is the figure nought, nothing
taken as written
taken as written
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone plays nothing in a closed car while making music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closed vehicle' looks like a saloon car, but 'closed' is a container signal: the first three pieces close round the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument, a source of music.

clue.text: Consider introducing new name for flavouring

indicators.note: the consider word has the two letters introduced into it

parts.note: to feel is to consider or believe

explanation.surface: Think about using a new name for a flavouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' places N and N in the middle of FEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fennel is an aniseed-flavoured herb used as a flavouring in cooking.

clue.text: Show one's hand in decision on policy?

definitions.text: Show one's hand in decision on policy?

parts.words: Show one's hand in decision on policy?
parts.note: showing one's hand looks like revealing cards, but here it is raising a hand to be counted when a policy is decided

explanation.definitionFit: Raising a hand in a meeting is a way of casting one's choice on a motion, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Erase recent broadcast primarily about new rite

indicators.note: primarily says the broadcast abbreviation comes first in the answer

parts.note: OB stands for outside broadcast

indicators.note: the word for recent goes about, around, the rearranged rite

parts.note: something recent is late, as in the late news

indicators.note: a new version of the word rite has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Delete the latest broadcast, which mainly concerned a new religious rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' does not take a first letter here; it says the outside-broadcast abbreviation comes first, with 'new' an anagram signal inside 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate something is to wipe it out completely, a stronger synonym of erase.

clue.text: Old, good English painter

parts.note: pi is short for pious, i.e. good

explanation.surface: An old English painter of some merit.
explanation.definitionFit: John Opie was an eighteenth-century Cornish portrait painter, so a named example.

clue.text: Glides along smoothly and wins races

parts.note: a car or skater that sweeps along moves smoothly and swiftly
a winner takes the prize

explanation.surface: A horse glides smoothly along and wins its races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'races' looks like part of the picture of winning, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweepstakes are races, especially horse races, in which the prize is the pooled stakes.

clue.text: Trendy-sounding place to stay

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for trendy is heard, giving one of the same sound

parts.note: something trendy is in, fashionable

explanation.surface: A fashionable-sounding spot to stay the night.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub offering lodging, a place for travellers to stay.

clue.text: Try and eat stew, but rabbit on endlessly

indicators.note: to stew food is to cook it into a mix, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone tries to eat a stew but keeps chattering instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' suggests the meat for the stew, but rabbit on is British slang for talking at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To yatter is to chatter incessantly, the same idea as the British slang rabbit on endlessly.

clue.text: Possible cause of trouble on vessel crossing river?

definitions.text: Possible cause of trouble on vessel crossing river?

indicators.note: in an across clue, trouble on the vessel places the trouble word after it
the ship's letters cross the river, lying on either side of it

parts.note: SS is the prefix for a steamship
the Tay is a river in Scotland
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Something that could cause problems for a ship crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also wryly describes this sail as a possible source of trouble aboard; in an across clue 'on' puts the trouble after the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A staysail is a fore-and-aft sail set on a stay, part of a vessel's rigging.
